title: Distribute Candies Among Children II
summary: Given positive integers n and limit, calculate the total number of ways to distribute n candies among 3 children with each child receiving no more than limit candies.
statement: Given positive integers n and limit, calculate the total number of ways to distribute n candies among 3 children with each child receiving no more than limit candies.
constraints: n and limit are positive integers.
Distribute all n identical candies among three distinct children.
Count assignments where every child receives at most limit candies.
hints: Unbounded three-child distributions are counted by stars and bars.
Apply inclusion-exclusion to assignments where one or more children exceed limit.
Compute C(n+2,2)-3C(n-limit+1,2)+3C(n-2limit,2), treating invalid combinations as zero.
Shifting an over-limit child down by limit+1 maps violations to smaller unrestricted compositions; inclusion-exclusion corrects their overlaps exactly.
editorial: Shifting an over-limit child down by limit+1 maps violations to smaller unrestricted compositions; inclusion-exclusion corrects their overlaps exactly.

tests.explanation: The valid distributions are the three permutations of (1,2,2).
All ten nonnegative three-part compositions of three respect the limit.
